_doc: Near-miss stems that must NOT trigger their rule. >=5 per wording rule.
A test set of obvious positives alone proves nothing: an implementation
that flagged every coordinator, every 不, or every capitalised word would
pass the positives and then produce a useless false-positive rate on real
questionnaires. These negatives are the only thing keeping the rules
honest, and they are the cases a naive implementation gets wrong.
Both language versions are checked, so both must be non-triggering.

double_barreled.why: 「您和家人」is who the respondent was with, not two judged targets. Splitting changes the question: it is about eating together.

stem.zh-CN: 您和家人一起用餐的频率是？
stem.en: How often do you eat out with your family?

double_barreled.why: The coordinator joins the respondent to a companion; neither side is an evaluation object.

stem.zh-CN: 您与朋友讨论过本产品吗？
stem.en: Have you discussed this product with friends?

double_barreled.why: Subject of a single shared action, not two evaluated targets.

stem.zh-CN: 您和您的同事是否共用同一个账号？
stem.en: Do you and your colleagues share one account?

double_barreled.why: 「质量和价格的比值」is one concept. Split it and one half stops meaning anything.

stem.zh-CN: 您如何评价质量和价格的比值？
stem.en: How would you rate the ratio between price and quality?

double_barreled.why: The relationship between the two is itself the single object of judgement.

stem.zh-CN: 您认为价格与质量之间的关系是否合理？
stem.en: Is the relationship between price and quality reasonable?

double_barreled.why: Value for money is one established construct.

stem.zh-CN: 请评价本产品的性价比。
stem.en: How would you rate the value for money?

double_barreled.why: 「都」makes it one conjoined claim: have you used BOTH. Splitting changes the proposition.

stem.zh-CN: 线上和线下渠道您都使用过吗？
stem.en: Have you used both online and offline channels?

double_barreled.why: Work and study are the setting, and 「都」asks whether both settings apply at once.

stem.zh-CN: 您在工作和学习场景中都会使用它吗？
stem.en: Do you use it both at work and while studying?

double_barreled.why: 「同时」/ both asks about the joint consideration, which is one behaviour.

stem.zh-CN: 您购买时会同时考虑价格和质量吗？
stem.en: Do you consider both price and quality when buying?

double_barreled.why: Control: one evaluation object, no coordinator at all. Must never fire.

stem.zh-CN: 您平时更关注配送速度吗？
stem.en: Do you usually care more about delivery speed?

leading_question.why: Asks for an evaluation without supplying one.

stem.zh-CN: 您如何评价本次服务？
stem.en: How would you rate this service?

leading_question.why: Asks whether the price is reasonable rather than asserting it is.

stem.zh-CN: 您认为这个价格是否合理？
stem.en: Do you think this price is reasonable?

leading_question.why: Contains 同意 but presents no position to agree with; a naive marker list catches this.

stem.zh-CN: 您是否同意以下说法？
stem.en: Do you agree with the following statement?

leading_question.why: An open invitation carries no valence.

stem.zh-CN: 请评价本产品的整体表现。
stem.en: Please rate the overall performance of this product.

leading_question.why: Asks about problems without asserting that any occurred: a negative topic is not a leading frame.

stem.zh-CN: 您在使用过程中遇到过问题吗？
stem.en: Did you run into any problems while using it?

double_negative.why: Two negations, but in different clauses, so the reader never has to unwind them together.

stem.zh-CN: 这个功能不错，价格也没有问题。
stem.en: The feature is fine, and the price is no problem.

double_negative.why: 不同 is one ordinary compound, not a negation of the verb.

stem.zh-CN: 您对不同方案的偏好是什么？
stem.en: Which of the different options do you prefer?

double_negative.why: 不仅 is a discourse connective; treating every 不 as a negation would fire here.

stem.zh-CN: 不仅如此，您还会推荐我们吗？
stem.en: Beyond that, would you recommend us?

double_negative.why: 不错 means good. A naive negation count reads it as a negation.

stem.zh-CN: 您觉得这个设计不错吗？
stem.en: Do you think this design is good?

double_negative.why: One negation is plain and readable; only stacking is the problem.

stem.zh-CN: 这个功能对您没有帮助吗？
stem.en: Is this feature not useful to you?

absolute_wording.why: 通常 / usually is a hedge, the opposite of an absolute.

stem.zh-CN: 您通常多久使用一次本产品？
stem.en: How often do you usually use this product?

absolute_wording.why: 一般 is a hedge and also a scale midpoint word.

stem.zh-CN: 您一般如何评价本次服务？
stem.en: In general, how do you rate this service?

absolute_wording.why: 大部分情况下 explicitly avoids the absolute claim.

stem.zh-CN: 大部分情况下您会选择哪种方式？
stem.en: In most cases, which option do you choose?

absolute_wording.why: 有时 / sometimes sits at the other end of the frequency range.

stem.zh-CN: 您有时会遇到配送延迟吗？
stem.en: Do you sometimes experience delivery delays?

absolute_wording.why: A plain count question carries no quantifier at all.

stem.zh-CN: 过去一个月您下过几次订单？
stem.en: How many orders did you place last month?

jargon.why: The acronym is glossed in brackets on first use, which is exactly the remedy the rule asks for.

stem.zh-CN: 本产品的 API（应用程序接口）是否好用？
stem.en: Is the interface easy to use?

jargon.why: Ordinary words for an ordinary process.

stem.zh-CN: 您如何评价我们的服务流程？
stem.en: How do you rate our service process?

jargon.why: Describes the action rather than naming a metric for it.

stem.zh-CN: 您觉得下单过程是否顺畅？
stem.en: Was placing an order straightforward?

stem.zh-CN: 您对配送时间满意吗？
stem.en: Are you happy with the delivery time?

jargon.why: An ordinary capitalised word at the start of a sentence must not be read as an acronym.

stem.zh-CN: 您会再次购买本产品吗？
stem.en: Would you buy this product again?

question_length.why: 39 characters: just inside the Chinese guideline, so an off-by-one would show up here.

stem.zh-CN: 综合考虑您本次购物的整体体验，请问您对我们的服务是否感到满意呢？
stem.en: Are you satisfied overall?

question_length.why: 24 words: just inside the English guideline.

stem.zh-CN: 满意吗？
stem.en: Considering the delivery time and nothing else about your recent order with us, how satisfied would you say you are right now?

question_length.why: A short stem, the normal case.

stem.zh-CN: 您对本次配送是否满意？
stem.en: Are you happy with this delivery?

stem.zh-CN: 您的年龄段是？
stem.en: Which age group are you in?

question_length.why: A mid-length stem that a tighter limit would wrongly catch.

stem.zh-CN: 请问您最近三个月内是否使用过本产品的退换货服务？
stem.en: Have you used the returns service in the past three months?

fabricated_citation.why: A year in the stem is a time reference, not a citation.

stem.zh-CN: 2026 年您是否使用过本产品？
stem.en: Did you use this product during 2026?

fabricated_citation.why: Brackets carrying an answering instruction must not read as a reference.

stem.zh-CN: 请选择您的年龄段（可多选）。
stem.en: Choose your age group (multiple answers allowed).

fabricated_citation.why: A year plus a number is still not an author-year pattern.

stem.zh-CN: 您在 2025 年的消费金额大约是多少？
stem.en: Roughly how much did you spend in 2025?

fabricated_citation.why: A bracketed hint with a capitalised word inside but no year.

stem.zh-CN: 请在下方填写您的建议（选填）。
stem.en: Write your suggestion below (Optional).

fabricated_citation.why: Asks where the respondent heard about the product; mentions a source without citing literature.

stem.zh-CN: 您是从哪个渠道了解到本产品的？
stem.en: Where did you first hear about this product?
